questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was very close to Berlin which is a city I've always wanted to live in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the international office was very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: An employee of the International office sat down with me for half an hour and explained me everything I needed to know.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I think I was very lucky as I got my accommodation through a friend. Otherwise WG-gesucht or the Facebook group Danskere i Berlin.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you live in Berlin, it can be quite a commute. Sometimes the trains strike.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was mostly made difficult by my home university and the fact that the registration process in Germany was very foreign to me.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get the course catalog 2 weeks before the start of the semester and then there is a week where you can attend whichever courses you find interesting and then a couple of weeks where you can deregister for the ones you don't want.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office, the professors

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do as many classes in the first week as you can. And look out for the exam requirements. Some have very hard exams and some are just passed by regular attendance. Sometimes you can choose to just get 3 ECTS and then just attend the class without having to take the exam at the end. I think I would have preferred to take more classes and then have no exams at the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was different to the one I am used to at my home university. I found them a lot more discussion based.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. In some classes the professors barely participated but instead had us do many group presentations. In some cases it worked well, but generally I think I would have gained better insight into the various topics by having a professor teach me.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Regionale Integration im Internationalen Vergleich
Autoritärer Föderalismus: Russland im Vergleich
Forced Migration: Aufnahme und Integrationspolitik in der EU
Die Erweiterungspolitik in der Europäischen Union 
Democracy Under Pressure

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Any courses with Stanislav Klimovich. I think he mostly teaches in German, but the courses are super interesting!

questions.answer: Food is generally pretty cheap. Movie tickets too.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many different ones. I didn't get around to exploring any of them though.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't try any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The park Sanssouci is really beautiful. The lakes in the Potsdam area are also beautiful. Many pretty places to walk like Grunewald

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found it pretty easy to just ask people about things I was unsure of in class and made friends that way. It will probably be easier if you speak German.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any to be honest

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It is a very flexible education system and the professors are generally really chill.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Take more courses than you think you need. Maybe you can avoid taking exams at the end

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The administration is generally very helpful and respond really quickly

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a lot of new people both through uni and elsewhere.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Taking courses in German

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
